newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Aug 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Aug 19.

text.p: THE DOMINION

Teen drink figure 'the same for children': A survey that shows that more than a quarter of teenagers between the ages of 14 and 18 are heavy drinkers could have found the same result in children as young as 12, according to the Alcohol Liquor Advisory Council. Page 1.

British keen to return Maori head: Liverpool City Council, which unearthed a preserved Maori head from a grave, has said it will take every step to ensure that the head is returned to the New Zealand government. Page 1.
Super adverts draw complaint: The Alliance has lodged a complaint with the Advertising Standards Complaints Board against radio advertisements about the proposed retirement savings scheme. Page 2.

Williamson to launch promotional cards: Communications Minister Maurice Williamson will launch a phone card at a Wellington service station today despite claims the card is really a scratch-and-win game that will encourage children to gamble. Page 2.
Cabinet considers buildings: The Cabinet was still considering proposals for ministerial accommodation, a spokeswoman for Ministerial Services Minister Don McKinnon said on Monday. Page 2.
Market not quick to heed bank: Financial markets seemed to test the Reserve Bank's nerve on Monday after the central bank warned monetary conditions were too loose. Page 13.

Wilson and Horton profit up though revenue slows: New Zealand Herald publisher Wilson and Horton has increased its interim after-tax profit by 17.1 percent to $21.3 million despite only a slight increase in revenue. Page 13.

Panel finds ignorance about funds: Fund managers and retirement income providers are not doing enough to explain how their businesses work, according to independent referendum panel chairman Sir John Robertson. Page 13.
THRE PRESS
Police drop death charge: Police on Monday dropped a manslaughter charge against the manager of Wicked Willies nightclub after a private investigator found flaws in the police case. Page 1.

Peters' chances 'slim': Treasurer Winston Peters is likely to fail in any attempt to challenge the Winebox Inquiry findings, even though some of the tax transactions investigated were morally questionable, legal experts say. Page 2.

Bradford predicts lower electricity prices: Energy Minister Max Bradford is forecasting lower power prices next year as government measures start to bite and competition comes into the retail market. Page 3.

FCL Energy likely to star: Better-than-expected production from the Maui field plus an abnormal gain is expected to boost Fletcher Challenge Energy's net profit to around $260 million when it reports on Wednesday. Page 21.
BIL criticised over agm venue: Brierley Investments Ltd has been accused of staging its annual meeting in Napier to avoid difficult questions from shareholders. Page 22.
Netscape seeking NZ content partners: Internet software company Netscape Communications Corporation is seeking partnerships with New Zealand media companies for content. Page 22.
Positive re-rating for NZI Insurance: The claims-paying ability of NZI Insurance has been re-rated to AA from AA-minus by international ratings agency Standard and Poor's. Page 22.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD

Greens lay down law to Alliance: The Greens want all Alliance candidates to run under an "Alliance-Green" banner at the next election -- a demand causing some conflict in multiparty talks resuming today at Parliament.

Peters strikes deal, strikes out: Winston Peters, in Balclutha at the weekend for a regional meeting of NZ First, was tackled over his election campaign pledges to restore services to Balclutha Hospital, which is due to be demolished and replaced with a health centre.
Business support for tax changes: Business leaders support Sir Ronald Davison's main recommendations for taxation changes arising from the Winebox investigation.

Millennium bug vigilance advised: Prudent organisations were taking a close look at their suppliers and customers to prevent infection with the millennium computer bug, ANZ Bank chief executive Ralph Norris said.
Telecom holds the keys: Communications Minister Maurice Williamson supports self-regulation in the telecommunications industry, but not if that just means one player is ganged up on by the rest.
Deal clears skies for more British flights: British Airways will add more code sharing services to and from New Zealand following a new air services agreement between the two countries.

Williamson's stand fails to convince Clear, BellSouth: For something that Communications Minister Maurice Williamson dismisses as academic, the ownership of the telephone numbering system generates considerable heat among new-entrant telephone companies.
